task_instance: Create a small sample .burp-style project scenario and use the skill's burp-search.sh wrapper to extract audit findings / proxy history headers from it (the skill's core stated deliverable: searching/extracting data from a Burp Suite project file via the burpsuite-project-file-parser extension running inside Burp Suite Professional).
blocker_detail: The skill explicitly states it 'delegates parsing to Burp Suite Professional - it does not parse .burp files directly' and requires (1) Burp Suite Professional installed, headless-invokable via `"$BURP_JAVA" -jar -Djava.awt.headless=true "$BURP_JAR" --project-file=...`, and (2) the third-party burpsuite-project-file-parser extension JAR loaded into it via Burp's Extender UI. Burp Suite Professional is commercial, licensed software that requires purchasing a license and a PortSwigger account to download/activate (https://portswigger.net/burp/pro) - it is not obtainable via a package manager or free download. The runtime has Java (OpenJDK 21) but no burpsuite_pro.jar exists anywhere on the system, no BURP_JAVA/BURP_JAR env vars are set, and there is no `scripts/burp-search.sh` wrapper present in this benchmark's ce_sources tree to even inspect/run. Obtaining Burp Suite Pro would require a paid/account-bound service, which the safety rules explicitly forbid ('no account-bound or paid services'). Without Burp Suite Pro (and the extension loaded inside it), there is no way to parse or search a .burp project file at all - a raw .burp file's internal format is not documented/stable for independent parsing, and the skill itself makes clear this is intentional (it is a thin CLI wrapper around Burp's own extension API, not a standalone parser).
evidence: Checked runtime: `which java` -> /usr/bin/java (OpenJDK 21.0.10) present. `which burpsuite burp` -> no output (not installed). `find / -iname '*burp*'` -> no burpsuite_pro.jar or burp-search.sh found anywhere on the filesystem outside the SKILL.md itself. `echo $BURP_JAVA $BURP_JAR` -> both empty. Read SKILL.md in full: it states under Prerequisites that Burp Suite Professional must be installed from portswigger.net/burp/pro (a paid commercial product) plus a third-party extension JAR loaded through Burp's GUI Extender tab, and the 'Manual Invocation' section confirms the only way to run the parser is by shelling out to a real burpsuite_pro.jar. No free/open-source substitute is offered by the skill (it explicitly is not a standalone .burp parser). Concluded the task cannot proceed past this prerequisite without a paid PortSwigger license/account, which the safety rules forbid, so stopped here per the task's blocker-recording instructions instead of attempting a workaround.
